newsitem.title: USA: Allergan's Zorac gets German approval.
newsitem.headline: Allergan's Zorac gets German approval.

text.p: Allergan Inc Thursday said it received approval from the German Ministry of Health to market Zorac topical gels to treat mild-to-moderate plaque psoriasis.

In a statement, the company said Zorac is the first topical, receptor-selective retinoid to be marketed for this indication. The product is currently awaiting premarket clearance from the U.S. FDA for the treatment of plaque psoriasis and acne.
Psoriasis, which affects one to three percent of the world's population, is an incurable skin disorder characterized by thick, scaly plaques on the skin surface.

Allergan said extensive clinical trials, reviewed by the German Ministry of Health, have shown treatment success rates of up to 70 percent in patients treated with Zorac once daily. For many patients, some clinical benefit was maintained for up to 12 weeks after treatment was stopped. The primary side effects observed were transient, mild-to-moderate manifestations of local irritation which were manageable, the company said.
